question: What does the manual say group riding requires from each participant, besides motorcycle readiness?
choice_a: A CB radio installed on every motorcycle
choice_b: A matching motorcycle make and model
choice_c: At least five years of riding experience
choice_d: An alert mind free from worries, distractions, stress, and the influence of alcohol or drugs
explanation: Riding with a group requires an alert mind free from worries, distractions, and stress, and riding free from the influence of alcohol or drugs -- even too much caffeine or prescription medication can affect concentration.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.35, 'Group Riding: Preparation'

question: What should a group discuss during a hand-signal review at the rider's meeting before a group ride?
choice_a: The common hand signals so all riders can communicate during the ride
choice_b: Only who will pay for gas
choice_c: The exact top speed each rider intends to reach
choice_d: Hand signals are not used in group motorcycle riding
explanation: During the rider's meeting, review the hand signals so all riders can communicate during the ride; a diagram of common hand signals is included at the end of the manual.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.35, 'Hand Signals'

question: If a rider falls behind during a group ride, what should the rest of the group do?
choice_a: The group should speed up to finish the route faster
choice_b: Everyone should slow down to keep the group together
choice_c: The lead rider should turn around alone to find them
choice_d: The group should split permanently into two rides
explanation: During the ride, use your mirrors to keep an eye on the rider behind and confirm the group is staying together; if a rider falls behind, everyone should slow down to keep the group together.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.35, 'Observe Those Behind'

question: Why does the manual say riders should never ride directly alongside another rider in the same lane (pairing up)?
choice_a: Pairing up is illegal only on divided highways
choice_b: It is more fuel-efficient to ride single file
choice_c: There is no place to go if you have to maneuver to avoid a car or hazard in the roadway
choice_d: It has no real downside as long as both riders are experienced
explanation: Never ride directly alongside another rider in the same lane -- there is no place to go if you have to maneuver to avoid a car or hazard in the roadway. Wait until both are stopped to talk.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.35, 'Don't Pair Up'

question: In a staggered formation, where does the group leader ride, and where does the second rider position?
choice_a: Formation position is left entirely to each rider's preference
choice_b: The leader rides in the center of the lane; all other riders follow directly behind in single file
choice_c: The leader rides in the right side of the lane; the second rider rides directly alongside
choice_d: The leader rides in the left side of the lane; the second rider stays at least one second back in the right side of the lane
explanation: In a staggered formation, the group leader rides in the left side of the lane, and the second rider stays at least one second back and rides in the right side of the lane, with the pattern continuing at two-second intervals for later riders.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.36, 'Staggered Formation'

question: When should a group move to single-file formation?
choice_a: When riding in curves, turning, or entering and leaving freeways or highways
choice_b: Only when the group has more than ten riders
choice_c: Single file is used only for parking, never while moving
choice_d: Never -- staggered formation should be used at all times
explanation: It is best to move to single-file formation when riding in curves, turning, and entering or leaving freeways or highways, being sure to keep a proper following distance.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.35-36, 'Group Riding'

question: At an intersection with a left-turn signal arrow, how should a group handle the turn?
choice_a: Turn side-by-side to clear the intersection faster
choice_b: Tighten the formation and turn single file, stopping at a safe point if not all riders get through
choice_c: Have the last rider run the red light to keep the group together
choice_d: Split into two separate turning lanes regardless of markings
explanation: Intersections present the highest risk for motorcyclists in a group. When making a left turn with a signal arrow, tighten the formation to allow as many riders through as possible, turning single file -- if not all riders get through, stop at a safe point and wait rather than feeling pressured to run the light.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.36, 'Intersections'

question: When entering an interstate or freeway as a group, how should riders merge?
choice_a: All riders should merge simultaneously side-by-side
choice_b: Merge in staggered formation immediately upon entering the ramp
choice_c: Enter in single file and form up into staggered formation only after all riders have safely merged
choice_d: Freeway merging rules don't apply to group rides
explanation: A staggered formation is essential on freeways and interstates, but riders should enter in single file and form up only after all riders have safely merged in traffic.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.36, 'Interstate Highways and Freeways'

question: When a staggered-formation group passes slower traffic on a two-lane highway, how should the pass be conducted?
choice_a: Passing in formation on a two-lane highway is never attempted
choice_b: The entire group should pass simultaneously, side-by-side
choice_c: Only the lead rider is permitted to ever pass
choice_d: Riders should pass one at a time, each returning to their original lane position to open room for the next rider
explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders in a staggered formation should pass one at a time. After passing, each rider should return to their original position to open room for the next rider, since conditions may have changed even if the earlier rider passed safely.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.36-37, 'Passing in Formation'

question: According to the "Ten Rules of Group Riding," the length of the route and its segments should be based on:
choice_a: The ability of the least experienced rider
choice_b: The ability of the most experienced rider
choice_c: The fastest motorcycle in the group
choice_d: Whichever rider is leading that day
explanation: The Ten Rules of Group Riding include basing the length of the route and segments on the ability of the least experienced rider, and adjusting the pace through curves to that rider's ability.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.37, 'Ten Rules of Group Riding'

question: According to the manual, the most important rules for group riding include no competition, no tailgating, and:
choice_c: No use of headlights during the day
explanation: The most important rules for group riding are: no competition, no passing of other riders, and no tailgating. If a rider insists on riding faster, allow them to go ahead to an agreed meeting point.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.35, 'Group Riding'

question: Where should inexperienced riders be positioned within a group?
choice_a: In front of the leader, setting the pace
choice_b: At the very back of the group, unsupervised
choice_c: Just behind the leader, so they don't have to chase the group and more experienced riders can watch them from behind
choice_d: Position within the group makes no difference
explanation: Place inexperienced riders just behind the leader. This ensures they won't have to chase after the group, and the more experienced riders can watch them from the back.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.35, 'Group Riding'
